title: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Against Covert Misalignment
topic: Social Aspects->Fairness, Equity, Justice and Safety
claim: A two-stage automated framework reframes hidden objectives and evolves evasion strategies, turning a flagged trajectory into one that passes monitoring.
layout: 3 stacked rows, left-to-right flow, benign failure on top, evasion success below
description: The figure has three horizontal bands. The top band shows the task setup. On the left are a user query (main task) and a system prompt (side task), each with an icon. Beside them is a baseline agent trace with a monitor response, marked by a red X, where the monitor flags the hidden secondary task with a 98.7 verdict. The middle band is the method pipeline. Stage 1, Intention Concealment, takes a Relationship module (four icons: nec, method, comp, verify) and reformulates the side task. A plus sign leads into a Strategy Bank with trace obfuscation and monitor interference strategy boxes. Stage 2, CoT Evasion, is a genetic search with fitness criteria and crossover/mutation nodes. The bottom band shows the TraceMRT agent trace and the monitor's low verdict, marked by a green check. Red and blue italic text highlights key trace phrases.
caption: Overview of the TraceMRT framework. In Stage 1, Intention Concealment reframes the secondary task as a legitimate sub-goal of the primary task, iteratively refining the prompt via self-consistency verification to ensure faithful intent concealment without omissions. In Stage 2, CoT Evasion runs a genetic search over trace-obfuscation and monitor-interference strategies, evolving candidate strategy pairs by interpretation fidelity and strategic suitability before selecting the top-performing candidate trajectories for final evaluation against the target CoT monitor across tasks.
abstract: As LLM agents advance rapidly in autonomy, the risk of hidden objectives that bypass safety constraints becomes increasingly plausible. Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring offers a key control mechanism by reading the agent's reasoning and flagging misalignment before it materializes into action, yet its reliability depends on the realism of the red-team it is stress-tested against. Existing red-teaming efforts rely on shared templates, such as casting a side task as a prerequisite, which treat the side objective as an exogenous insertion and leave task-specific, contextually grounded evasions underexplored. We therefore ask: How robust is CoT monitoring against agents that strategically conceal misalignment? To answer this, we introduce TraceMRT, an automated Trace-level Monitor Red-Teaming framework that reframes the side task as a coherent sub-goal of the primary task and searches trace-shaping strategies whose induced trajectories complete the misaligned objective while reading as natural execution. Through black-box attacks on state-of-the-art monitors such as GPT-5.2 and Claude-4.5, we reveal substantial vulnerabilities even in top models. To counter these vulnerabilities, we propose a Bayesian Trajectory Monitoring framework, integrating global context and local segment evidence to detect covert misalignment. Empirically, our method significantly consolidates monitor robustness with 0.91 AUC and 0.74 TPR@FPR=0.05.
